idea: 015 Seven hedged pairs: fade a 20-day z-score stretch (scout ideas 1, 3 and 4 as one basket)
hypothesis: When the log price of a hedged pair of related markets (two currencies of one bloc against the dollar, gold against silver, one equity index against another) closes at 16:00 New York at least 2 standard deviations away from the mean of its 20 previous 16:00 values, it moves back toward that mean over the next 1 to 5 trading days by more than the two legs' costs.
mechanism: The two legs share their macro drivers; a stretch of the pair over days comes mostly from one-sided flow (hedging, issuance, sector rotation, silver's thinner market) that is not information and fades. Market-neutral against the dollar or the equity market, held over days: not the closed families 'night mean reversion on FX crosses' (round 6, intraday hours), 'index relative strength intraday' or 'lead-lag between markets'. Round 4's BLOC_MR was dropped before any test; the lab never tested two-legged spreads over days. Lead's ruling (CHARTER 'Rulings' (a)): scout ideas 1, 3 and 4 are ONE rule, run as ONE basket of seven pairs, each pair one market.

data.signal: prices only: the legs' prepared hourly BID bars (kit.data.load_bars, ~/explore_data/h1, aggregated from the lab's one-minute Dukascopy BID bars). Daily value of a pair = log of (close_a / close_b) for a ratio, log of (close_a x close_b) for a product, from the two legs' BID closes of the hourly bar that OPENS at 15:00 New York wall-clock time (DST-correct, Monday to Friday), i.e. the bar that closes at 16:00 New York; KNOWN at that bar's end = 16:00 New York (20:00 or 21:00 UTC). A day counts only if BOTH legs have that bar.
data.publication_lag: none: no external series; every value is a bar close known at the bar's end (bars indexed by their open, row length 1 h in the truncation test).
data.prices: kit.data.load_bars(<fp key>) = prepared H1 BID bars 2013-2021 for eurusd, gbpusd, audusd, nzdusd, usdchf, usdcad, xauusd, xagusd, us100, us30, ger40, us500; pairs by kit.sim.pair_book (ratio: P = a/b, long = long a short b; product: P = a x b, long = long both); equal notional per leg
data.in_sample_years: 2013-2021 (9 years; us100/us30 and ger40/us500 from 2013-11, us30 and ger40 bars start 2013-09/10). Power check from the signal data alone (the pair's own z, no return): days with |z| >= 2: 361 to 410 per pair; first crossings of 2: 147 to 184 per pair; a flat-gated count with the z exit or 5 days gives about 140 to 168 entries per pair, about 1,060 in all on about 850 distinct entry days: the basket bars can be reached.

rule_main.signal: per pair, c_d = the daily value above on each day d where both legs have the 15:00-NY bar; z_d = (c_d - mean(c over the 20 previous such days)) / sample std (ddof 1) of those 20 values (current day never in the window); known_at = 16:00 New York of day d (end of the 15:00-NY bar). Every day with |z_d| >= 2 is a signal (one position per pair: a signal while the pair holds a trade is skipped).
rule_main.side: -sign(z): z >= +2 sells the pair (ratio: short a, long b; product: short both), z <= -2 buys it
rule_main.entry: open of the first H1 bar of the pair (both legs) opening at or after known_at (normally the 16:00-NY bar)
exit: z back inside +/-0.5: events = known_at of every day with |z_d| <= 0.5 (16:00 NY), per pair; the trade leaves at the open of the first bar at or after the first event strictly after its entry bar's open
rule_main.overlap: one position per pair (kit.sim mode 'one'); every-signal variant for the every-signal bar

changes_vs_scout: None of substance. Made explicit: the 16:00-NY value is the BID close of the 15:00-16:00 NY hourly bar of each leg (mid would differ by the modelled spread only); days missing either leg's 15:00-NY bar (holidays, index closures, data gaps) are not in the 20-day window; the stop and D20 follow kit.sim.PairBook (the pair is observed at bar opens and closes only, D20 from those observations, a stop is filled at the observation that crosses it, not at the level); the 5-trading-day maximum is pandas BDay from the entry bar (kit 'bdays'); scout ideas 3 and 4 used the same parameters and are merged per the lead's ruling.
costs: kit.costs (lab/r2/fp_costs.json, FP Raw), each leg its own spread (bp of its reference price x hour-of-week shape), slippage and swap (side held on each leg); gross, net, spread and slippage x1.5
bars: CHARTER.md 'The bars' for a BASKET of 7 pairs (each pair one market) on 01_main, computed by kit.judge.verdict: t on daily sums >= 2.5, pooled PF >= 1.12 and >= 1.04 at costs x1.5, >= 60 % of years positive, >= 65 % of pairs positive, no pair above 25 % of the profit, neighbours' median PF >= 1.06, every-signal expectancy > 0, hold <= 5 trading days, random-entry null (same-day for pairs decided at the same 16:00 NY time) >= 97.5th percentile with 2000 draws and the main's own exit, events and stop; truncation tests of the signal build and the event build with the default cuts; weekly corr with the ten <= 0.30; deflated Sharpe on N_all (label). Reported apart, not judged: each pair, the three groups (currency crosses, metals, indices), long and short sides, gross figures.
split: IS only (to 2021-12-31). No VAL look in this run (lead's instruction); if every IS bar passes, the attack of charter rule 5 (attack.py) is done and the lead does the VAL look.
